key_insight: The Trajectory Alignment Coefficient (TAC) is a practical metric that quantifies how closely a reward function's induced trajectory preferences match desired behavior, and can be used both to guide reward-weight tuning and as an objective to learn reward functions from data.
problem_solved: Designing reward functions is time-consuming and error-prone; TAC gives practitioners a diagnostic and optimization tool to detect and correct misspecification so learned policies better align with task intent.
method: Define TAC: measure alignment between rankings (or preference orderings) of trajectories induced by a candidate reward and those representing task intent (e.g., demonstrations, specs, or expert preferences).

Two acts: (a) Reward tuning — use TAC to select or tune reward weights that increase alignment without full RL retraining; (b) Reward learning — optimize reward parameters directly to maximize TAC using demonstrations/preferences as a reference.
Empirically validate TAC-guided tuning and learning on benchmark tasks, showing improved policy alignment and reduced manual tuning effort compared to baseline approaches.
impact: TAC gives ML practitioners a lightweight, interpretable signal to detect and fix reward misspecification and to automate reward learning, reducing iteration time and improving alignment between learned policies and human intent.
visual_elements: Schematic: pipeline showing two acts — (1) Reward tuning guided by TAC, (2) Reward learning optimizing TAC — with arrows from reward → trajectories → TAC score.
Bar/line chart: TAC score vs. policy performance and vs. number of tuning iterations to show correlation and speed-up.
Heatmap or matrix: pairwise trajectory preference alignments under ground-truth vs candidate rewards to visualize where mismatches occur.
Icon set: short icons for 'metric' (TAC), 'tuning' (slider), 'learning' (gear/gradient), and 'human intent' (person or demo) to emphasize practitioner workflow.
paper_title: The Trajectory Alignment Coefficient in Two Acts: From Reward Tuning to Reward Learning
paper_authors: Calarina Muslimani, Yunshu Du, Kenta Kawamoto, Kaushik Subramanian, Peter Stone
